# Aspire Conventions

> **Related skill:** to wire a new host, queue, inter-domain call, third-party stub or E2E scenario into Aspire, invoke
> [`coreex-aspire`](/.github/skills/coreex-aspire/SKILL.md). This file holds the invariants that must hold on **any** edit to
> an `aspire/**` file. For the full narrative see [Aspire & End-to-End](/.github/docs/coreex/aspire.md) (docs-sync cache).

## Project roles

| Project | Role | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `*.Aspire` (AppHost) | Declares hosts + their dependencies; runs them together with a dashboard | Wiring only — no business logic, no DI registrations for the hosts |
| `*.Aspire.MockHost` | WireMock.Net console host that stands in for HTTP dependencies **outside** the AppHost | Started via `AddMockHostProject`; carries no stubs itself — stubs are added by the test (or at AppHost start) |
| `*.Test.Aspire` | NUnit project deriving `WithAspireTester<Projects.X_Aspire>`; starts the whole AppHost and asserts cross-host flows | The **only** place inter-domain dependencies are real |

`dotnet new coreex-aspire` generates all three; the `AddEndpoints` / `AddHostedServiceSupport` / `DisableHttpCertificateValidation` /
`AddMockHostProject` / `WithMockHostEnvironment` / `HttpMock` helpers come from `CoreEx.UnitTesting` + `UnitTestEx.Aspire`
(`<Using Include="UnitTestEx.Aspire" />` in the AppHost csproj) — there is no local `Extensions.cs`.

## AppHost wiring

Infrastructure (databases, Redis, Service Bus emulator) runs from `docker-compose.yml`, **not** Aspire. Model it as connection-string resources whose
names match what each host passes to its client-integration package; then add one `AddProject` per host, referencing only what it needs.

```csharp
var serviceBus = builder.AddConnectionString("ServiceBus").WithIconName("MailMultiple");

var productsApi = builder.AddProject<Projects.Contoso_Products_Api>("products-api")
    .WithReference(postgres).WithReference(redis).AddEndpoints("/health/ready/detailed");

builder.AddProject<Projects.Contoso_Products_Subscribe>("products-subscribe")
    .WithReference(postgres).WithReference(redis).WithReference(serviceBus)
    .AddEndpoints("/health/ready/detailed").AddHostedServiceSupport();   // relay + subscribe hosts always get hosted-service support
```

- Resource names are kebab-case `{domain}-{host}` (`products-api`, `shopping-subscribe`). They are the names used by `Test.Http("products-api")`, `WaitForResourceAsync`, and service discovery — never rename casually.
- Each new host needs a `<ProjectReference>` in the AppHost csproj (this is what generates `Projects.X`).
- Relay: data provider + Service Bus. Subscribe: data provider + Redis + Service Bus. Api: data provider + Redis (+ Service Bus only if it publishes directly, not via outbox).

## HTTP calls outside the domain

A host that calls something outside itself falls into exactly one of three cases. Pick by *where the callee lives*, never by convenience.

| Callee | Wire it with | Test.Aspire |
|---|---|---|
| **Another domain in the same AppHost** (e.g. Shopping → Products API) | `.WithReference(calleeApi)` on **every calling host**; the caller's `appsettings.Development.json` sets `BaseAddress` to `https+http://{resource-name}` and the client is registered with `builder.AddTypedHttpClient<XxxHttpClient>("ConfigSection")` | Real call — **no stub**. Just wait for the callee (`WaitForResourceAsync`) |
| **Third-party API** (SendGrid, payment gateway, …) | `var mockhost = builder.AddMockHostProject<Projects.X_Aspire_MockHost>("mock-host");` then `.WithMockHostEnvironment("SendGrid__BaseAddress", mockhost, "http")` on **every calling host** (this overrides the configured `BaseAddress`) | Stub in `OnAfterStartAsync` (below) |
| **Another domain that is *not* in this AppHost** (separate repo/solution) | Treat as third-party: MockHost + `WithMockHostEnvironment`, stubbing that domain's HTTP contract | Stub in `OnAfterStartAsync` |

```csharp
// AppHost.cs — third-party API stood up by the MockHost.
var mockhost = builder.AddMockHostProject<Projects.Contoso_Aspire_MockHost>("mock-host");
builder.AddProject<Projects.Contoso_Shopping_Subscribe>("shopping-subscribe")
    /* ...references... */
    .WithMockHostEnvironment("SendGrid__BaseAddress", mockhost, "http");
```

```csharp
// Test.Aspire — stub the third-party route once the MockHost is running.
protected override async Task OnAfterStartAsync(DistributedApplication app)
{
    await app.WaitForResourceAsync(["products-api", "shopping-api"]);
    await app.HttpMock("mock-host", "http").Request(HttpMethod.Post, "/v3/mail/send").WithAnyBody().Respond.WithAsync(HttpStatusCode.Accepted);
}
```

- The `WithMockHostEnvironment` key is the configuration path with `__` separators and must match the section the typed client reads (`AddTypedHttpClient<T>("SendGrid")` reads `SendGrid:BaseAddress`).
- The AppHost-scaffolded `mockhost` line is commented out until a stub is genuinely needed — uncomment it, do not add a second MockHost.
- Auth material for a third-party client (`ApiKey` etc.) must still resolve to *something* in `appsettings.Development.json`, or the typed-client factory throws before the call reaches the mock.
- Never call the real third-party API from Aspire tests. Never stub an intra-AppHost domain — that hides the very integration Aspire exists to verify.

## Test.Aspire lifecycle

`WithAspireTester<T>` starts the AppHost between two hooks. The `Test.*` migrate/reset helpers of the intra-domain testers are **not** available here — use the `app.*` equivalents.

```csharp
public class E2ETest : WithAspireTester<Projects.Contoso_Aspire>
{
    protected override async Task OnBeforeStartAsync(DistributedApplication app)
    {
        // Runs BEFORE any host starts: seed state and create broker entities so receivers/relays find them on startup.
        await app.MigratePostgresDataAsync<Products.Test.Common.TestData>("Postgres", ["mutate-data.seed.yaml"], Products.Database.Program.ConfigureMigrationArgs);
        await app.ClearRedisCacheAsync("redis");
        await app.ResetAzureServiceBusAsync("ServiceBus", ServiceBus.GetQueues(), ServiceBus.GetTopicsAndSubscriptions());
    }

    protected override async Task OnAfterStartAsync(DistributedApplication app)
        => await app.WaitForResourceAsync(["products-api", "shopping-api"]);   // + HttpMock stubs (above)
}
```

- **Service Bus topology is code**, in a static `ServiceBus` class (`GetQueues()` / `GetTopicsAndSubscriptions()`). A single-domain solution reuses its `Test.Common` `ServiceBus`; a multi-domain AppHost owns one **union** class listing every domain's topic, subscriptions **and command queues**. A queue that is missing here makes the relay fail to send and the command receiver fail to start.
- Command queues are `RequiresSession = true` (the receivers are session receivers); topic subscriptions likewise.
- Drive flows over real HTTP with `Test.Http<T>("resource-name")`. For anything asynchronous (outbox → relay → broker → subscriber) **poll with a bounded loop** (`Test.Delay(1000, "reason")` up to N attempts, then `Assert.Fail`) until the observable effect appears; assert a stubbed third-party call with `Test.AssertLogContains("UnitTestEx > Sending HTTP request", "mock-host")`.
- The Aspire tester has no broker-peek helper. A command's delivery to its queue is proven in `*.Test.Relay` (`GetAndClearAzureServiceBusAsync`); Aspire proves the *effect* in the consuming host.

## Do Not

- Do not run infrastructure through Aspire (`AddPostgres`, `AddRedis`, `AddAzureServiceBus`) — the emulators come from `docker-compose.yml`.
- Do not hard-code ports or URLs in tests or `BaseAddress` — use resource names / service discovery.
- Do not put business logic, migrations or seed data in the AppHost.
- Do not use `[OneTimeSetUp]` for AppHost preparation — the hooks are `OnBeforeStartAsync` / `OnAfterStartAsync`.
- Do not stub an HTTP dependency that is itself a resource in the AppHost.
